title: Delivered and 'acknowledged' - but the reply is from someone other than the patient
summary: A walk-in critical result is delivered by SMS with a receipt. A reply arrives from the registered number and the gateway marks it as an acknowledgment from a verified number. The words of the reply say it is from the patient's daughter, and that the patient is in hospital abroad. The structured record says the patient acknowledged; the person did not. Rules read the structured fields and close the case. A safe system must read what was said, not record the communication, and hand the case to a person.

research_questions: What evidence of identity does an SMS reply carry, and who may acknowledge a critical result on a patient's behalf (gap GR-09)?
